verdict.rationale: Maritime publishes dedicated framework pages for Claude Code and Codex. They describe running Claude Code in its own always-on cloud micro-VM with persistent storage, and running Codex on Maritime's metered LLM access with no key required, which together form a first-party recipe for hosting these coding agents. Templates are pre-configured and deploy from a single image pull. Missing for 10: step-by-step recipe details (setup steps and isolation guarantees) quoted in the evidence, and independent or hands-on corroboration that Claude Code and Codex run as described.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can run coding agents like Claude Code or Codex inside the sandbox following the vendor's own recipe

citations.quote: Maritime gives it what a laptop session can't: its own always-on micro-VM in the cloud, persistent storage, sleep/wake economics, and every chat channel Maritime supports.
No key is required: the agent uses Maritime's metered LLM access by default.
Every ready-made template is a real agent framework, pre-configured and one image pull from live.
